body:
### Additional regression behaviors in chunk-based TileMap physics with `one_way_collision = true`

I can confirm this regression in Godot 4.5 and would like to document **two distinct issues** that appear after the introduction of chunk-based TileMap physics.  
Both have significant gameplay impact for 2D platformers migrating from 4.4.x to 4.5.

---

### 1. Internal diagonal edges treated as walkable slopes
When multiple one-way tiles are merged into a chunk, the convex decomposition step generates **internal diagonal edges** to split the polygon into convex shapes.  
Currently, these internal edges are registered in the physics engine as **real, walkable collision surfaces**.  
When the player moves or falls toward such an internal diagonal, the character is guided **up or along the line** as if it were an actual slope, instead of staying on the intended flat/stepped surface.  
> These internal diagonals are not visible in the TileMap artwork, but they exist in the merged collision shapes and affect movement.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c7b6b864-65a5-41b3-bd11-d0a5a2e2b838

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/06a8b65f-93c3-4573-ab5f-4dccd0181108

---

### 2. Loss of per-tile landing surfaces in vertical stacks  
In 4.4.x (tile-by-tile collisions), stacking multiple single-collision tiles vertically allowed the player to **land on intermediate or bottom tiles** when falling straight down, as each tile's top surface was an independent landing contact.  
In 4.5 (chunk-based physics), **internal horizontal boundaries between adjacent tiles are removed** during merging:  
- The top faces of **intermediate and bottom** tiles are no longer considered valid landing surfaces.  
- The physics engine only keeps the **outermost** boundary, causing these internal landing points to be ignored.  
This changes level flow and character control in ways that can break existing platformer designs.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/826e7442-849f-4981-b6d0-c7d46c35419d

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/52d838f6-b825-43c9-bc3f-5063b462a902

---

### Migration impact
These changes have **major impact** for 2D platformers migrating from 4.4 to 4.5:
- **One-way platforms**: internal diagonals alter landing/pass-through and slope behavior.
- **Per-tile stairs / multi-layer landing**: intermediate surfaces are lost, changing fall and climb pacing.
- **Level feel and control**: collision routes, edge cases, and player pathing can break, leading to softlocks, unintended slowdown, or invalid routes.
For many existing projects, collision data and movement code would require substantial rework.

---

### Repro steps / typical use case: one-way drop-through with multi-layer landing
1. Create two TileMap layers:
   - **Drop layer tiles**: one-way platforms (on physics layer `DROP_LAYER`).
   - **Ground layer tiles**: solid ground (on `GROUND_LAYER`).
2. In the drop layer, vertically stack ≥3 rectangular one-way tiles in the same column so that they appear as "middle" and "bottom" platforms.
3. Implement player control to temporarily disable collisions with the drop layer when pressing the "drop" key:
   ```gdscript
   # On drop key press:
   player.set_collision_mask_value(DROP_LAYER, false)
   # On drop key release:
   player.set_collision_mask_value(DROP_LAYER, true)
Place the player above the topmost platform and test vertical falling:

4.4.x: Player can land on the middle platform or continue down to the bottom platform depending on mask switching.

4.5: Internal collision boundaries between stacked tiles are gone; middle/bottom tiles are ignored as landing surfaces — only the outermost boundary is considered.

Expected: Even with chunk-based merging, the engine should preserve per-tile landing detection for one-way + collision-mask-based drop-through mechanics.

Suggestion
Consider adding merge modes similar to Unity's Tilemap Collider + Composite Collider:

Outline: merge into a smooth outer outline (good for ground/platforms).

Polygon: preserve original tile shapes and their individual boundaries (good for stairs, multi-layer landings, and one-way platforms).

### MRP:tilemap_chunk_oneway_regression_demo.zip

[tilemap_chunk_oneway_regression_demo.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21790404/tilemap_chunk_oneway_regression_demo.zip)

The one_way_collision flags are still present and active.

It seems they now detect collision edges beyond just the outer outline. With chunk merging, the original per-tile edges are gone, which naturally leads to unexpected behavior. If an internal diagonal is generated, it also becomes part of the collision detection.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ed4f5824-187c-4470-bb62-167391d5f2ac
Ah that's a good find. I didn't think about that situation. I'll see if I can figure out a way to avoid merging those cells vertically if they use `one_way_collision`.
You can work this around by changing the one-way collider to take half of the tile:

> You can work this around by changing the one-way collider to take half of the tile: > > Thanks! This workaround (using half-tile one-way colliders) really helps for now. I can confirm it solves the issue in my project until the proper fix is implemented.

> Ah that's a good find. I didn't think about that situation. I'll see if I can figure out a way to avoid merging those cells vertically if they use `one_way_collision`.

Thanks a lot for looking into this!

I just wanted to share a small thought: completely disabling merging for one-way tiles would indeed solve the regression and restore the expected behavior from 4.4.x. The only concern I can imagine is that it might slightly increase the number of collision shapes when many one-way tiles are used in larger areas.

In practice, though, most projects only use one-way platforms in smaller or isolated sections (rather than across huge continuous regions), so the performance impact should usually be minor. Still, perhaps in the longer term it could be nice to have a configurable merge mode (similar to Unity’s “Outline” vs. “Polygon” option), so developers can choose between performance and preserving per-tile collisions depending on their needs.

Either way, thank you for working on this — I really appreciate the attention to detail and backward compatibility.

>  so developers can choose between performance and preserving per-tile collisions depending on their needs.

You can already switch between the two. If you reduce the physics quadrant size to 1, you have one collision body per cell.
